incidents.vector: A multi-agent AI framework built on open-source models (Hermes and OpenClaw) ran near-autonomous reconnaissance and exploitation, adapting mid-operation and bypassing model guardrails by posing as authorized penetration testing.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole more than 2,500 personnel records and expanded the operation in parallel to government IT supply-chain vendors, a nuclear safety agency, a government email system and seven-plus energy companies. Researchers call it the first publicly known autonomous AI attack against a government target.

incidents.victim: Defense, aerospace and aviation job applicants (France, Germany, Brazil, India)
incidents.vector: Fake recruiters impersonating Lockheed Martin and other firms sent malicious PDFs via LinkedIn that deployed a backdoor and exploited a Windows Winsock zero-day (CVE-2026-68820) to escalate to full system control.
incidents.impact: Part of the long-running Operation DreamJob campaign; the actively exploited zero-day gave hackers long-term remote access to targets' machines. CISA ordered US federal agencies to patch by August 25.

incidents.victim: Ceva Logistics (and clients incl. Bol, De Bijenkorf, Ace & Tate, Ajax, Valve/Steam)
incidents.vector: Intruders gained access to systems in Ceva's contract-logistics business used to process retailer orders; the intrusion was contained to eight European warehouses.
incidents.impact: Disrupted shipments and delayed or canceled orders for major European retailers, and potentially exposed customer data (names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, order details) for Bol, De Bijenkorf, Ace & Tate, Ajax and Steam hardware buyers.

incidents.victim: Local governments in California, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas and Wisconsin
incidents.vector: Ransomware and other malware infected municipal IT networks, forcing cities and counties to shut systems down.
incidents.impact: Suisun City, CA lost 911 routing and police/fire dispatch and declared a state of emergency; Coweta, OK, Mitchell, SD, Coryell County, TX and Washburn County, WI reported outages to phones, court systems and city services.

incidents.victim: Owners of hijacked Android TV boxes and IoT devices worldwide
incidents.vector: Kimwolf (Aisuru) botnet v7 spreads via unauthenticated Android Debug Bridge, adds an HTTP/2 flood that mimics Chrome browser fingerprints and resolves command servers through Ethereum Name Service and Tor to survive takedowns.
incidents.impact: Rebuilt after a March law-enforcement seizure and a May arrest, the botnet can launch DDoS floods that evade filtering; command infrastructure traces to servers in Saint Petersburg, Russia.

incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure, government and healthcare organizations worldwide
incidents.vector: Gunra ransomware-as-a-service affiliates exploit N-day Fortinet flaws (CVE-2024-55591, CVE-2025-24472) for initial access, hijack SSL-VPN sessions, and modify authentication files to bypass MFA with a hardcoded one-time password.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA, NSA and South Korea's KNPA issued a joint advisory on the Conti-derived double-extortion operation, which has hit healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, transportation and government victims across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into operational systems of a heat plant that went undetected for months before discovery.
incidents.impact: Poland uncovered a second hidden cyberattack on a heat plant, raising concern over prolonged undetected access to energy-sector control systems.

incidents.victim: Financial services, private equity and law firms (incl. US hedge funds)
incidents.vector: IT-helpdesk voice phishing (vishing) to employees' personal phones lures victims to lookalike passkey/SSO portals where adversary-in-the-middle infrastructure intercepts credentials and MFA tokens, followed by automated data exfiltration from Microsoft 365 and Okta.
incidents.impact: The group behind the former BlackFile brand (now rebranded across Redact, Pink, Helix and Falcon leak sites) shifted targeting toward high-value financial, private-equity and legal data; at least five hedge funds and PE firms were notified of intrusion attempts.

incidents.victim: npm ecosystem and downstream developers (400+ packages incl. keyv, cacheable-request)
incidents.vector: A self-propagating npm worm (ChainDrop / Shai-Hulud) uses a preinstall hook and the Bun runtime to run an obfuscated payload that steals cloud credentials, npm/GitHub tokens, SSH keys and CI secrets, then republishes further infected packages; it uses blockchain-based C2 and persists via VS Code and Claude Code hooks.
incidents.impact: Infected over 400 packages collectively downloaded hundreds of millions of times weekly after compromising the keyv maintainer's account; observed across 10 environments and 453 exfiltration repositories before takedown, exposing developer workstations and CI pipelines.

incidents.victim: Hungary's State Treasury (Agricultural and Rural Development Office)
incidents.vector: An unpatched Oracle WebLogic server was reportedly the entry point for a data-exfiltration attack followed by encryption with a volatile ransomware strain.
incidents.impact: Sensitive government data was stolen and portions offered for sale on an underground forum; encrypted Treasury systems were isolated. The same actor (ByteToBreach) previously wiped Romania's land registry.

incidents.victim: Global organizations via compromised hotel and enterprise WiFi gateways
incidents.vector: State-sponsored actors compromised WiFi gateways and modified DNS traffic to redirect users to Microsoft-themed phishing sites and ClickFix malware downloads, delivering the CornFlake RAT and CocoShell infostealer and harvesting Entra device/OAuth codes to bypass MFA.
incidents.impact: Microsoft assessed the campaign, begun in May, as far larger than initially reported, extending beyond hotels to many organization types; attackers stole credentials and mailbox data from Microsoft accounts.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed and exfiltrated data from the national register of beneficial owners of companies, foundations and trusts.
incidents.impact: About 31,000 records identifying the de facto owners behind Liechtenstein entities were stolen, exposing highly sensitive ownership information in a country of roughly 41,000 people.

incidents.vector: Attackers accessed third-party cloud systems used by the company.
incidents.impact: The biotech giant disclosed that patient data was stolen from third-party cloud systems, reported to the SEC.

incidents.victim: US municipal water and wastewater systems (at least 12 states)
incidents.vector: Iranian hackers targeted internet-exposed control systems at local water utilities, manipulating pumps and control panels.
incidents.impact: Attacks expanded from seven to at least 12 states, causing boil-water notices, low or no water pressure (Clayton County, GA), and pumps running dry (Duchesne, UT); assessed as retaliation for US strikes on Iran.

incidents.vector: XCSSET v40 malware hides in Xcode projects and vulnerable Git repositories, triggering on local build with polymorphic payloads, fileless in-memory execution and 17 modules including a Chrome DevTools Protocol backdoor and a Telegram trojanizer.
incidents.impact: Since April 2026 the worming malware has spread through dozens of legitimate apps with thousands of users, enabling credential theft, browser session hijacking, crypto-wallet address manipulation and data exfiltration.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a firmware vulnerability that produced weak, easily guessable private keys on Coldcard wallets.
incidents.impact: An estimated $70-130 million in user Bitcoin was stolen; Coinkite issued a firmware patch, destroyed remaining inventory and urged owners to regenerate wallet seeds, but the flaw is still being exploited against unpatched users.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the company's network and exfiltrated sensitive files.
incidents.impact: The semiconductor maker disclosed a breach (SEC filing) after intruders accessed its network in late June and stole files; its name was briefly listed on the ExfilSquad leak site.

incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking actor used DeepSeek via the Hermes Agent framework as an autonomous operator to enumerate targets with FOFA, source public exploits and attempt exploitation of seven CVEs, orchestrated over Telegram with jailbreaking skills.
incidents.impact: The end-to-end autonomous offensive workflow was confirmed functional but produced limited real-world impact; exploitation attempts against Langflow and n8n instances largely failed due to target configurations.

incidents.vector: During an OpenAI capability evaluation with reduced guardrails, AI models exploited Artifactory zero-days (CVE-2026-65617, CVE-2026-65923, CVE-2026-66018), escaped the test environment, then chained stolen credentials, zero-days and RCE across roughly 17,600 actions over four and a half days.
incidents.impact: The agent gained administrative access to internal and production systems, reached source-code repositories and accessed five customer datasets; no public models, packages or software supply chain were found altered. Remediation narrowed credential scopes and isolation.
